why: There are no multi-step Plans, only individual Tasks.
example: An operator sends a multi-step plan to the Asset.

why: A restart on the ground drops queued Tasks; nothing resumes on its own.

phrase: \blive reference\b|\bas it stands when it gets there\b|\b(keeps? (its|the) original plan|follows? the new shape)\b|\b(reads?|gets?|obtains?) (the |that )?place'?s? current shape\b|\bnever copies the shape\b

why: A crashed Asset is inspected before its next flight.

phrase: \bstarts? the built-in safe action\b[^.]*\bfail-?safe command\b|\bfail-?safe command\b[^.]*\b(always )?(runs|starts) (the |its )?built-in safe action\b

phrase: \b(the app |service |it )?restarts? (itself|the app|it) automatically\b|\bthe app restarts itself\b|\brestart(s|ed)? in flight\b|\bon startup\b[^.]*\b(airborne|flying)\b[^.]*\bfailsafe\b
why: Nothing restarts the Asset app on its own; an app that fails in flight stays down and the flight controller returns home.

phrase: \b(stopping core|every stop( of core)?|any stop( of core)?) is reset\b
why: Only a deliberate stop of Core is Reset; a crash or power loss resumes the run.
example: A run lasts from one start of Core to the next stop, and stopping Core is Reset.

why: Asset IDs are never reused, not even in a later run; when they run out, Core refuses new registrations and tells the admin.
example: Asset IDs start again each run, like Task numbers.

phrase: \bcritical\b[^.]*\b(falls? back to land|lands where it is)\b
why: A failed critical failsafe response falls back to Return to home, not Land.
example: A failed critical response falls back to Land.

why: An Asset signs up with its description only when its app starts, never on a reconnect.

why: Results an app had not reported before a restart on the ground are lost.

why: There is no clear count: a failure clears the queue, later Tasks run normally, and operators cancel what they don't want.

why: Failsafe rules have no separate missing- or stale-data conditions.
example: A measurement_stale condition covers an unknown position.

why: Each firing runs its response once; there is no configurable fallback, and priority does not only rise.
example: Each rule gets a primary attempt and one optional fallback.

why: If Core's Reset ZIP fails, Core keeps the data and tells the admin; it does not try again at later starts.
example: At every start, Core tries again to write the ZIP of each earlier run.

why: A crash while Core is stopping on purpose just resumes the run.
example: If Core crashes while stopping, the deliberate stop stands.

why: Core decides the 64-Task cap from the Asset's latest queue report; it keeps no capacity bookkeeping.

why: Dropped requests just show as not done; Core does not reconcile them when the Asset returns.

why: A failed Reset ZIP is kept and reported, never retried at a later start, for Core, Assets, and gateways.
